legend: You are given an array a$$$a$$$ of n$$$n$$$ non-negative integers, and a positive integer m$$$m$$$.
You need to answer q$$$q$$$ queries. In each query, you are given a non-negative integer x$$$x$$$.
You can do the following operation:

choose two integers 1≤l≤r≤n$$${1 \le l \le r \le n}$$$ such that r−l+1=m$$${r - l + 1 = m}$$$, and for each l≤i≤r$$${l \le i \le r}$$$ replace ai$$$a_i$$$ with ai | x$$${a_i \space | \space x}$$$. where x | y$$${x \space | \space y}$$$ denotes the bit-wise OR of x$$$x$$$ and y$$$y$$$.
For each query, output the minimum number of operations needed to make the elements of the array equal, or output −1$$$-1$$$ if they cannot be made equal.
input: The first line contains a single positive integer 1≤t≤3×105$$${1 \le t \le 3 \times 10^5}$$$ — the number of testcases.
The first line of each testcase contains two positive integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤m≤n≤106)$$${(1 \le m \le n \le 10^6)}$$$.
The next line contains n$$$n$$$ non-negative integers a1, a2, ..an$$${a_1, \space a_2, \space ..a_n}$$$ — the elements of array a$$$a$$$, where (0≤ai<230)$$$({0 \le a_i  \lt  2^{30}})$$$.
The next line contains a single positive integer q$$$q$$$ (1≤q≤106)$$${(1 \le q \le 10^6)}$$$ — the number of queries.
Each of the following q$$$q$$$ lines contains a single non-negative integer (0≤x<230)$$$({0 \le x  \lt  2^{30}})$$$.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n$$$n$$$ and q$$$q$$$ over all testcases does not exceed 106$$${10^6}$$$.
output: For each query of each testcase, output the answer to it as described in the problem statement.
